set.prevailing_wage_basis: False for the JPA conduit bond issuance itself: DIR Public Works Case No. 2006-001, Horizons at Indio (March 12, 2007), https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2007/2006-001.pdf, following PW 2004-016 Rancho Santa Fe Village, held that publicly offered multifamily housing revenue bonds issued by a conduit issuer (CSCDA), with proceeds and repayments assigned to a private trustee, are not a payment of public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(1) and are not a below-market public loan under 1720(b)(4); even if they were, the affordable housing loan exemption (40% of units at or below 80% AMI for 20 years, then 1720(c)(6)(E)) would apply. The County staff report for item 26-255 states CMFA debts are not obligations of the County, and the County only holds the TEFRA hearing. Applies to the bond issuance only; County AHF, HOME, CDBG, HACSM vouchers or other public money in the same deal is analyzed separately and can trigger state prevailing wage or Davis-Bacon.
set.audit_note: Tier 3: prevailing wage set false for the conduit bond issuance alone based on DIR coverage determination PW 2006-001 (consistent with other county bond records). Privately placed bond structures were not separately confirmed; layered public loans can still trigger coverage.

reason: DIR coverage determination PW 2006-001 holds that conduit-issued multifamily housing revenue bonds are not public funds under Labor Code 1720(b), so the CMFA, CSCDA or CEDA bond issuance alone does not trigger prevailing wage.
